title: Product Card 02 · Phase B Functional Website Components
thesis: Phase B applies the approved Round 10 visual grammar to real product-marketing and commerce interfaces. Round 03 recorded eleven keeps, thirty-five revisions and one kill; Round 04 rebuilt those revisions, retained the champions and removed B-FT06 alongside the earlier B-FT04 kill. Olli then approved every one of the forty-six Round 04 survivors as keep and closed H-EXP-04B-CARD-FUNCTIONAL-PROOF. The resulting fifteen components, thirteen website patterns and six journeys are canonical for their bounded design and interaction scope. The thirty-two Phase A keeps remain inherited visual authority. Illustrative prices, provider logic, golden-homepage selection and consumer-specific stress proof remain outside this component decision.

phaseAVisualInputs.authorityEffect: All thirty-two source expressions remain canonical approved Phase A visual inputs. Round 02 application feedback is preserved as evidence but does not create separate Round 04 candidates or alter Phase A approval.

functionalSpecimens.round04Treatment: Carry every Round 03 keep forward, rebuild every Round 03 revise from its named feedback, remove B-FT06, retain the earlier B-FT04 kill, and introduce no replacement specimens.
functionalSpecimens.lineageRule: Every surviving functional specimen preserves every approved Phase A reference recorded in the verbatim Round 02 and Round 03 receipts.

layers.name: Foundations and primitives
layers.purpose: Layout, controls, fields, feedback, focus, density and responsive behavior from the canonical foundation release.

layers.name: Product-expression adapters
layers.purpose: Round 10 identity, material, Wings, plate, card, bundle and motion grammar adapted to a functional job.

layers.name: Reusable components
layers.purpose: Stable semantic components with slots, state applicability, container behavior, accessibility and consumer events.

layers.name: Website composition patterns
layers.purpose: Heroes, menus, featured sections, explainers, bento, pricing, checkout, bundles and footers composed from reusable components.

layers.name: Journey fixtures
layers.purpose: Complete buyer and availability journeys that prove components work together without declaring a golden homepage.

semanticModels.name: Product
semanticModels.purpose: Stable product identity, public name, extended name, summary, availability and gradient assignment.

semanticModels.name: Availability
semanticModels.purpose: Truthful live, coming-soon, waitlist, unavailable and sold-out behavior.

semanticModels.name: Offer
semanticModels.purpose: One-time, subscription, usage, bundle, enterprise, trial, waitlist, free and add-on offers without inventing production pricing.

semanticModels.name: Price
semanticModels.purpose: Amount, currency, cadence, tax status, discount and disclosure supplied by the consumer.

semanticModels.name: Plan
semanticModels.purpose: Tier, included capabilities, limits, recommendation and billing options for SaaS scenarios.

semanticModels.name: Bundle
semanticModels.purpose: Included, optional and unavailable products plus bundle savings and selection rules.

semanticModels.name: LineItem
semanticModels.purpose: Product, bundle, add-on, discount, tax, credit and total rows.

semanticModels.name: ProofRecord
semanticModels.purpose: Claim, input, mechanism, changed state, result, verification, limitation and evidence class.

semanticModels.name: Action
semanticModels.purpose: Semantic label, intent, hierarchy, destination or callback and disabled reason.

semanticModels.name: Media
semanticModels.purpose: Static material, one focal live core, screenshot, proof artifact or absent media.

semanticModels.name: Checkout
semanticModels.purpose: Checkout state and provider slots without network calls, Stripe ownership or payment logic inside the component.

semanticModels.name: CommerceState
semanticModels.purpose: Empty, partial, ready, processing, confirmed, failed, cancelled and refunded lifecycle.

semanticModels.name: MotionAllocation
semanticModels.purpose: One automatically live Deep Mineral focal plate with exact static twins everywhere else.

components.name: ProductDiscoveryCard
components.role: Introduce, compare or select one product without forcing a purchase decision.
components.accessibility: Use a single semantic link or selection control, visible focus and text-backed selection or availability.
components.motion: Only an isolated featured card may request the one focal live plate; repeated discovery cards are static.

components.name: ProductFeatureCard
components.role: Explain one capability, use case or mechanism with visible evidence.
components.accessibility: Evidence remains legible without hover and annotated media has equivalent text.
components.motion: Material may animate only when this is the selected focal feature; proof and copy stay still.

components.name: ProductProofCard
components.role: Render a typed ProofRecord without letting a quote impersonate mechanism or outcome evidence.
components.accessibility: Evidence class, date, source and limitations are available as text and not encoded by color alone.
components.motion: Proof stays static; an adjacent focal product plate may own the single live allocation.

components.name: ProductFeatureBento
components.role: Lay out typed feature and proof cells when their relationship benefits from a non-uniform grid.
components.accessibility: DOM order carries meaning independently of visual spans; compact receivers linearize without omission.
components.motion: At most one declared focal product-material cell may animate; every other cell is static.

components.name: ProductPricingCard
components.role: Present one truthful offer with the correct language and controls for its commercial model.
components.accessibility: Price cadence, recommendation and disabled reason are explicit text; the whole card is not a nested button.
components.motion: Pricing objects and comparisons are static; product material is an optional static identity field.

components.name: ProductPlanComparison
components.role: Compare plans, products or offers without hiding essential differences on mobile.
components.accessibility: Use semantic table relationships where tabular, preserve headings on compact receivers and never require horizontal swipe for essential facts.

components.name: ProductCheckoutSummary
components.role: Keep the selected offer, line items, total, disclosures and commitment action understandable throughout checkout.
components.accessibility: Totals are programmatically associated, async changes announce politely and processing prevents double submission.
components.motion: Checkout identity and price UI remain static.

components.name: ProductBundleOffer
components.role: Explain a fixed package, its relationship and its value as one purchasable offer.
components.accessibility: Included products and exclusions are text, selection is explicit and pack visuals are not the sole information source.
components.motion: Bundle contents are static; one isolated lead cover may receive focal motion outside repeated commerce contexts.

components.name: ProductBundleBuilder
components.role: Let a buyer choose eligible products while keeping price, availability and bundle rules visible.
components.accessibility: Selection uses native controls, changes announce totals and constraints explain why an item cannot be selected.
prohibited: layout reordering that changes source order

components.name: ProductUpsellRow
components.role: Offer one relevant addition without disguising consent or blocking the original purchase.
components.accessibility: Accept and decline are equally understandable, price delta is explicit and no option is preselected deceptively.

components.name: ProductMobileStickySummary
components.role: Persist the current decision and action after purchase intent without covering essential page content.
components.accessibility: Appears after intent, respects safe areas, retains a 48px target and never traps keyboard or screen-reader focus.
components.motion: Static only; entrance is a short control transition and is removed under reduced motion.

components.name: ProductFamilyMatrix
components.role: Compare the product family with equal geometry, truthful availability and future-product tolerance.
components.accessibility: Compact receivers preserve every product and comparison label in source order without swipe-only access.
components.motion: All repeated product material is static.

components.name: ProductMenuItem
components.role: Represent a product consistently inside simple menus, product mega-menus and mobile navigation.
components.accessibility: Uses one link or button, current product is announced and submenu state follows the site-menu keyboard pattern.

components.name: ProductFooterCTA
components.role: Close a product, family or bundle page with one clear next action and stable identity.
components.accessibility: Heading and action remain first in reading order and mobile uses a full-width primary action.
components.motion: One isolated product field may animate automatically; footer navigation and controls remain static.

components.name: ProductPurchaseConfirmation
components.role: Confirm a completed purchase, explain access or next steps and preserve receipt clarity.
components.accessibility: Success is announced once, focus moves to the confirmation heading and access instructions do not rely on email alone.
components.motion: Static only; no celebratory motion is required for comprehension.

patterns.name: SingleProductHero
patterns.role: Open one product page with product-first hierarchy, one proposition and one focal product field.
patterns.proofRequirement: The hero must identify the product job or visible outcome, not only show material.
patterns.responsive: Compact receivers preserve title, extended name, action and media source order.

patterns.name: ProductFamilyHero
patterns.role: Introduce the product family while preserving equal product weight and live-product-first commerce.
patterns.proofRequirement: Every product must have a truthful job and availability state.
patterns.responsive: Vertical catalogue on compact receivers; no swipe-only roster.

patterns.name: ProductMegaMenu
patterns.role: Expose product discovery from global navigation without becoming a mini landing page.
patterns.proofRequirement: Optional proof must be literal and subordinate to navigation.
patterns.responsive: Collapses into a keyboard-safe mobile sheet with the same item order.

patterns.name: FeaturedProductSection
patterns.role: Feature one product or capability in a realistic marketing section.
patterns.proofRequirement: The section must connect claim, mechanism and visible evidence.
patterns.responsive: Copy remains ahead of supporting media when that preserves comprehension.

patterns.name: ProductExplainer
patterns.role: Explain how a product works as a sequence, architecture or comparison.
patterns.proofRequirement: Each step names input, action and result or explicitly states what is illustrative.
patterns.responsive: Preserve causal source order and visible step labels.

patterns.name: FeatureProofBento
patterns.role: Compose a meaningful non-uniform field of product, proof, workflow, metric, media, integration, quote and action cells.
patterns.proofRequirement: Every cell declares its job and evidence class; filler cells are invalid.
patterns.responsive: Grid spans collapse into a complete, logical linear reading order.

patterns.name: ProductFamilyShelf
patterns.role: Browse multiple products as one authored family.
patterns.proofRequirement: Each product carries a distinct job, canonical identity and truthful availability.
patterns.responsive: Compact receivers use a vertical catalogue; essential products are not hidden behind a carousel.

patterns.name: MultiPricingSection
patterns.role: Present one-time, SaaS, bundle or multi-tier decisions using the appropriate commercial language.
patterns.proofRequirement: Every offer is marked as production data or illustrative fixture and carries complete cadence and disclosure.
patterns.responsive: Plans stack, comparison remains accessible and the recommended treatment never changes source order.

patterns.name: ProductComparison
patterns.role: Compare products, offers or plans at a decision point.
patterns.proofRequirement: Comparison criteria must be factual, defined and complete enough to support the decision.
patterns.responsive: Use disclosure or stacked labelled groups rather than essential horizontal overflow.

patterns.name: CheckoutLayout
patterns.role: Compose consumer-owned checkout fields and provider slots around a stable Mez order summary.
patterns.proofRequirement: The chosen offer, total, tax status, action and recovery path remain visible.
patterns.responsive: Collapse to one decision column with the summary adjacent to the commitment action.

patterns.name: BundleSection
patterns.role: Present a fixed or configurable bundle in a realistic marketing and commerce context.
patterns.proofRequirement: Included products, exclusions, availability and selection effects are explicit.
patterns.responsive: Pack visuals simplify before selection or pricing information is removed.

patterns.name: UpsellCrossSellSection
patterns.role: Offer relevant additions before or after purchase without dark patterns.
patterns.proofRequirement: The incremental value and price delta are specific and truthful.
patterns.responsive: Accept and decline remain equally reachable on compact receivers.

patterns.name: ProductFooter
patterns.role: Close product-aware pages with stable parent identity, useful links and a bounded conversion moment.
patterns.proofRequirement: Links and endorsement are real; conversion copy matches current availability and offer data.
patterns.responsive: Link groups disclose or stack without changing information order.

journeys.name: Multi-product discovery
journeys.scenario: Browse an extensible family, compare jobs and availability, then open one product.
journeys.fixtureAuthority: canonical product identity plus illustrative navigation state

journeys.name: One-time digital purchase
journeys.scenario: Discover a digital product, evaluate one offer, checkout, process payment and receive access.

journeys.name: SaaS tier selection
journeys.scenario: Compare recurring tiers, choose billing interval and plan, hand off to checkout and confirm onboarding.
journeys.fixtureAuthority: illustrative SaaS product and commercial data only

journeys.name: Configurable bundle purchase
journeys.scenario: Choose eligible products, understand bundle rules, review the running summary and purchase the bundle.
journeys.fixtureAuthority: canonical product identity plus illustrative bundle and commercial data

journeys.name: Mixed availability and waitlist
journeys.scenario: Browse live and coming-soon products, enter a waitlist path and receive truthful confirmation.
journeys.fixtureAuthority: canonical current availability plus illustrative waitlist interaction

journeys.name: Mobile purchase, upsell and confirmation
journeys.scenario: Complete a narrow-screen purchase with sticky summaries, an optional addition and a clear success state.
journeys.fixtureAuthority: illustrative commercial and checkout data only

rules: container behavior owns the component before page viewport
family collections become vertical on compact receivers
essential comparison content is never swipe-only
sticky summaries appear only after purchase intent
safe areas and 48px touch targets are mandatory

eligible: one focal hero or feature field
one isolated lead bundle cover outside repeated commerce
motion.fallback: Exact static twin with no layout shift under reduced motion, no WebGL or runtime failure.

rounds.title: Models and component architecture
rounds.deliverable: Internal semantic models, reusable contracts and composition rules that support the rendered review candidates.

rounds.title: Functional breadth · Round 01
rounds.deliverable: Forty-eight rendered functional specimens established the functional breadth; review scope then expanded to include every approved Phase A survivor as an application study.

rounds.title: Phase A application plus functional breadth · Round 02
rounds.deliverable: Round 02 collected feedback on thirty-two Phase A application views and forty-eight functional specimens. Its application views are evidence only; the canonical Phase A keeps remain visual inputs.

rounds.title: Functional feedback convergence · Round 03
rounds.deliverable: The exact receipt records eleven keeps, thirty-five revisions and one kill across forty-seven candidates. B-FT06 was killed; B-FT04 remained absent from the earlier Round 02 kill.

rounds.title: Functional feedback convergence · Round 04
rounds.deliverable: Olli kept all forty-six functional survivors across six families. B-FT04 and B-FT06 remain absent; the thirty-two Phase A keeps remain inherited visual inputs rather than duplicate candidates.

rounds.title: State and responsive proof
rounds.deliverable: The reviewed workbench proves representative interaction, one-live-core motion, static fallback, equal geometry, mobile compositions, clean export and no desktop overflow or console failures. Exhaustive consumer-specific container, zoom, keyboard and content-stress matrices continue under EXP-08 and consumer proof rather than blocking this bounded approval.

rounds.title: Candidate lock
rounds.deliverable: All forty-six validator-passing survivors received keep. H-EXP-04B-CARD-FUNCTIONAL-PROOF closed through DEC-PRODUCT-COMPONENT-SYSTEM-001; the programme is canonical 1.0.0 for its bounded component scope.

convergenceRules: all forty-six Round 04 survivors are approved keeps
all forty-six survivors preserve every Phase A reference
unrelated component roles do not compete for one global winner
the thirty-two canonical Phase A keeps remain approved visual inputs and are not Phase B candidates
future revisions require a new named gate

required: forty-six unanimously kept Round 04 functional specimens
thirty-two canonical Phase A visual inputs with zero Phase B candidate count
verbatim Round 01 through Round 04 feedback hashes
complete Phase A lineage preserved for every survivor

System Editions and trading-card collector framing

workbench.note: Product Card 02 Phase B is canonical 1.0.0 through H-EXP-04B-CARD-FUNCTIONAL-PROOF and DEC-PRODUCT-COMPONENT-SYSTEM-001. All forty-six Round 04 survivors are approved keeps; B-FT04 and B-FT06 remain killed. The workbench is a locked proof record, not a new candidate round.
